title: The starter is the bakery
thesis: The slow invisible part of the work decides the result, long before anyone sees it.

nodes.text: If the starter is weak, the loaves come out flat and sour, and nobody can fix that at the oven.
Team work runs the same way: the slow invisible part decides the result long before anyone sees it.
The result is fixed before the visible work starts: the month of feeding the starter comes before any loaf.

evidence.filled_by: brief must_include.0: the month of feeding the starter

nodes.text: People who know the craft judge by the slow work: "That was the moment she knew he would be good."
Invisible work builds up over years: the eleven years of notebooks.

evidence.filled_by: brief must_include.1: the eleven years of notebooks

nodes.text: The objection: leads reward visible output because it's the only thing they can measure, and slow groundwork can also be a place to hide.
What follows for a team lead: protect the unglamorous early work instead of waiting to judge at the oven.
How does a lead tell real groundwork from stalling? The brief raises no objection and gives no answer.
What exactly should a lead do to protect the early work? The purpose names the goal but not the practice.
